crypto_certificate_verification_justific:
Unmet. Project deployment and cleanup scripts explicitly disable TLS certificate verification. The OSMO role-assignment client sets `check_hostname = False` and `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE`. The Redis cleanup client uses `--tls --insecure` for authenticated requests. Certificate verification is therefore not enabled by default for all TLS connections.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/infrastructure/setup/03-deploy-osmo.sh

Secrets and credentials are supplied through environment variables, GitHub Actions Secrets, managed identity/workload identity, Azure Key Vault, and deployment-time configuration, so rotation does not require rebuilding or recompiling.

crypto_keylength_justification:
Project-authored security mechanisms use a fixed 32-byte CSPRNG token and restrict JWT verification to RS256. Issuer key generation and TLS termination are external to the project.

crypto_password_storage_justification:
N/A. The project does not provide external-user password authentication. It does generate an optional PostgreSQL administrator password and writes it to Azure Key Vault; this is infrastructure credential generation rather than storage of external-user authentication passwords.

crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no key-agreement protocol. Provider-managed services terminate TLS and control key exchange, so perfect-forward-secrecy configuration is outside the produced software.
crypto_tls12_justification:
TLS-enabled Azure Storage resources require TLS 1.2. This evidence supports the configured Storage services only; it does not assert that every project network path uses TLS.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/infrastructure/terraform/modules/platform/storage.tf
crypto_used_network_justification:
Unmet. Although Azure Storage is configured for TLS 1.2, the default Azure ML extension setup sets `allow_insecure=true`, and the Dataviewer Container App explicitly sets `allow_insecure_connections = true`. These defaults do not support a claim that all network communications use secure protocols by default.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/infrastructure/setup/02-deploy-azureml-extension.sh
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/infrastructure/terraform/modules/dataviewer/container-apps.tf
crypto_verification_private_justificatio:
Unmet. The OSMO role-assignment request sends an `x-osmo-user: admin` header while certificate and hostname verification are disabled. The Redis cleanup client supplies authentication data while using `redis-cli --tls --insecure`. Private authentication and authorization information can therefore be sent before successful certificate verification.

Evidence:

repo_distributed_justification:
Git is a distributed version control system. Every clone of the repository contains the complete history and can function independently. Contributors fork and clone the repository (as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md), work locally, and submit changes via pull requests. There is no single point of failure — any clone contains the full repository history and can serve as a restore point.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
- https://git-scm.com/about/distributed
report_archive_justification:
GitHub Issues provides a permanent, public, searchable archive of all bug reports. Closed issues are retained indefinitely and remain accessible via search, filters, and direct URL. Issue history (comments, label changes, assignee changes, linked PRs, status transitions) is preserved. The archive is accessible without authentication. Issues can be filtered by label, milestone, date, author, and state (open/closed).

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/issues
report_process_justification:
Users can report bugs and issues via GitHub Issues, which are publicly accessible. The repository provides 7 structured issue templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ covering: bug reports, feature requests, documentation issues, security vulnerability reports, infrastructure requests, and more. Each template includes pre-defined labels, required fields, and guidance text. The process is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md (how to file) and SUPPORT.md (what to expect). Security vulnerabilities have a separate private reporting channel via SECURITY.md.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/issues
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE

report_tracker_justification:
GitHub Issues serves as the project's issue tracker. It is publicly readable, searchable, and filterable. Issues support labels, milestones, and assignees for triage and tracking. The 7 issue templates apply automatic labels for categorization. Closed issues remain in the searchable archive. The tracker is integrated with PRs via GitHub's "Fixes #NNN" linking, providing traceability from bug report to fix.

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j:
CodeQL runs with both "security-extended" and "security-and-quality" query suites — these are GitHub's most comprehensive security query sets, specifically designed to detect common vulnerabilities including: SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), path traversal, code injection, insecure deserialization, SSRF, hardcoded credentials, and other OWASP Top 10 categories. The security-extended suite goes beyond the default security queries to catch additional vulnerability patterns. Results are uploaded as SARIF to the GitHub Security tab, providing a centralized view of all detected security findings.

Evidence:
- https://github.com/microsoft/physical-ai-toolchain/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml

vulnerability_report_private_justificati:

The reporter is explicitly instructed NOT to report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues. Both channels are confidential — MSRC handles reports under their Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) policy, keeping details private until a fix is available. PGP key download is available at https://aka.ms/security.md/msrc/pgp.

The document explains what constitutes a security vulnerability, provides a PGP key for encrypted communication, references the Microsoft Bug Bounty program, and links to the Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) policy. This is the standard Microsoft OSS security reporting process used across thousands of Microsoft repositories.
